about: Me and the Boys uses a still from the 1960s Spider-Man cartoon showing four villains, Rhino, Vulture, Electro and the Green Goblin, crammed into one frame and grinning straight at the camera like friends posing for a group photo. The caption above them always starts with "me and the boys" and then names some oddly specific late-night mission. The humor comes from those smug, conspiratorial faces paired with a plan that is either completely harmless or wonderfully absurd, like hunting for beans at 3 am.
origin: "Me and the boys" was a sincere caption for group photos long before it became a joke. In 2019 ironic versions with nonsense follow-ups spread through Reddit and Instagram, and the version with the 1967 Spider-Man villains broke into the mainstream around late May 2019.
usage:
There is a single caption box above the image. Start with "me and the boys" (or "me and the boys at [time]") and finish with the scheme. The best captions are specific and a little ridiculous: an exact hour, a weird target, a petty goal.

Gaming squads, friend groups, coworkers on lunch break and students before an exam all fit. The villains' grins do the rest, so there is no need for a second punchline. Keep it to one line so the faces stay the focus.
ideas: me and the boys at 3 am looking for beans
me and the boys after the teacher says "any questions?" at 2:59
me and the boys pushing to prod on a friday
me and the boys queueing for one more ranked game at 4 am
me and the boys walking into the meeting with zero slides done
me and the boys when the pizza arrives at the office
aka: Spider-Man Villains Me and the Boys
